# mcloud sandbox

<!-- Generated by `go run ./internal/gendocs`: edit the source it names, not this file. -->

_Generated from the command's help in `internal/cli`._

[All commands](README.md)

Agent sessions: Claude Code in a sandbox in the cluster.

A session is Claude Code in a pod of its own in the cluster, under gVisor,
logged in with your Claude subscription. It can reach the internet, so it
can clone and install what it needs, and nothing in the cluster. Your own
files go in with start --from or cp, and its commits come back with pull.

Your sessions run in a sandbox that is yours alone: the first command here
makes it. It holds your Claude token (mcloud sandbox token set), which
only your own sessions read, and it limits how many sessions you can have
running.

  mcloud sandbox token set                 # once: the token claude setup-token prints
  mcloud sandbox start fix --from .        # a session with this directory in it
  mcloud sandbox prompt 'Fix the tests'    # one task, or: mcloud sandbox claude
  mcloud sandbox pull                      # its commits, into this repository
  mcloud sandbox ssh                       # SSH in (ssh-config: plain ssh, scp, rsync)
  mcloud sandbox stop fix                  # end it; its files go with it

## mcloud sandbox claude

Claude Code in a session.

Run Claude Code in a session: in the directory it was started --from, or
its work directory (/work). On a terminal it's the interactive interface;
what follows -- goes to claude as it is. SESSION can be left out when you
have one session. For a single task, see mcloud sandbox prompt.

Claude Code keeps its conversations in the session, so claude --resume and
--continue work for as long as the session does.

```
mcloud sandbox claude [SESSION] [-- ARGS...] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox claude
mcloud sandbox claude refactor -- --continue
mcloud sandbox claude -- -p 'Write fizzbuzz.js and run it' --permission-mode acceptEdits
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` string |  | the directory in the session to run in, relative to /work (default: what the session was started --from) |

## mcloud sandbox cp

Copy files into or out of a session.

Copy a file or a directory between this machine and a session. One of
SOURCE and DEST is SESSION:PATH, with PATH relative to the session's work
directory (/work). Like cp: the copy goes into DEST if that is a directory,
and is named DEST otherwise.

Coming out of a session, only files and directories are copied: links and
special files are left out, and nothing is written outside DEST. Git's own
files (.git) are left out too, since hooks and configuration in them would
run on your machine: mcloud sandbox pull brings a session's commits.

```
mcloud sandbox cp SOURCE DEST
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox cp ./my-repo refactor:my-repo
mcloud sandbox cp refactor:my-repo ./my-repo-after
mcloud sandbox cp notes.md refactor:
```

## mcloud sandbox forward

Open a session's ports on this machine.

Open ports of a session on this machine, until you stop it with Ctrl-C:
a dev server running in the session, in your own browser. PORT is the port
here; it reaches the same port in the session, or SESSION-PORT. SESSION
can be left out when you have one session.

Only this machine can use the ports (they listen on localhost), and they
reach only what listens on the session's own localhost. It is SSH's local
forwarding, set up for you: mcloud sandbox ssh has the details.

```
mcloud sandbox forward [SESSION] PORT[:SESSION-PORT]...
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox forward 5173              # http://localhost:5173 is the session's 5173
mcloud sandbox forward 8080:3000         # http://localhost:8080 is the session's 3000
mcloud sandbox forward refactor 3000 9229
```

## mcloud sandbox list

Your sessions.

```
mcloud sandbox list
```

## mcloud sandbox prompt

Give Claude Code in a session one task, and watch it work.

Give Claude Code in a session one task. What it does shows as it goes, its
answer comes last (on stdout, so it can be piped), and the command ends
when the task does. SESSION can be left out when you have one session.

Nobody is there to answer questions, so --permission-mode says what Claude
Code may do unasked. The default, auto, lets it edit files and run
commands, with its own check on each action; bypassPermissions takes that
check away, and acceptEdits allows edits only. What follows -- goes to
claude as it is.

--continue carries on from the session's last conversation.

```
mcloud sandbox prompt [SESSION] PROMPT [-- ARGS...] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox prompt 'Run the tests and fix what fails'
mcloud sandbox prompt refactor 'Now commit that' --continue
mcloud sandbox prompt 'Summarise this repository' > summary.md
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--continue` |  | carry on from the session's last conversation |
| `--dir` string |  | the directory in the session to run in, relative to /work (default: what the session was started --from) |
| `--permission-mode` string | `auto` | what Claude Code may do unasked: auto, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, plan |

## mcloud sandbox pull

Bring a session's commits into this git repository.

Fetch the commits a session has made into the git repository you're in.
Each branch of the session's repository arrives as sandbox/SESSION/BRANCH,
and the branch you're on moves forward to the session's branch of the same
name when it can (a fast-forward; --no-merge leaves it alone). From there
it's your own git: push, open a pull request.

Only commits come over: what the session hasn't committed stays there. The
session needs none of your git credentials for this, and gets none.

The session's repository is the directory it was started --from, or --dir.
SESSION can be left out when you have one session.

```
mcloud sandbox pull [SESSION] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox pull
mcloud sandbox pull refactor --no-merge
mcloud sandbox pull refactor --dir my-repo
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` string |  | the directory in the session to run in, relative to /work (default: what the session was started --from) |
| `--no-merge` |  | only fetch: leave the branch you're on where it is |

## mcloud sandbox remove

Delete your sandbox: its sessions, their files and your token.

Delete your sandbox: every session in it, their files, and your Claude
token. mcloud sandbox start makes a new, empty one.

```
mcloud sandbox remove [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes` |  | don't ask |

## mcloud sandbox shell

A shell in a session, or one command.

Open a shell in a session, or run what follows -- there: in the directory
the session was started --from, or its work directory (/work). SESSION can
be left out when you have one session.

```
mcloud sandbox shell [SESSION] [-- COMMAND...] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox shell
mcloud sandbox shell refactor -- git status
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` string |  | the directory in the session to run in, relative to /work (default: what the session was started --from) |

## mcloud sandbox ssh

SSH into a session.

Open a shell in a session over SSH: in the directory the session was
started --from, or its work directory (/work). What follows -- goes to ssh
as options, -L to open a port of the session's here, say. SESSION can be
left out when you have one session.

The connection goes through the cluster's API, like every other command
here: an exec of sshd in the session, with SSH over its input and output.
Nothing in the session listens, and you need nothing but your mcloud
login. mcloud logs in with a key of its own, and checks the session's
host key, which it reads from the session first. Your SSH agent, X11 and
remote forwarding (-R) are never forwarded: the session can't reach back
to your machine. -L reaches what listens on the session's own loopback,
nothing else.

For scp, rsync, sftp and editors that work over SSH, mcloud sandbox
ssh-config gives ssh a host name for every session. To only open a port,
mcloud sandbox forward is shorter.

```
mcloud sandbox ssh [SESSION] [-- SSH-OPTIONS...] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox ssh
mcloud sandbox ssh refactor -- -L 3000:localhost:3000
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` string |  | the directory in the session to run in, relative to /work (default: what the session was started --from) |

## mcloud sandbox ssh-config

SSH settings that make ssh, scp, rsync and editors reach sessions.

Print the ssh configuration that gives every session a host name:
SESSION.sbx for one of yours, SESSION.USER.sbx for USER's (an admin's
access). Then plain ssh works, and what runs over it: scp, rsync, sftp,
an editor's remote development over SSH, ssh -L.

  ssh refactor.sbx
  rsync -a refactor.sbx:my-repo/dist/ ./dist/
  ssh -N -L 3000:localhost:3000 refactor.sbx

--install writes it to a file of mcloud's and includes that at the top of
~/.ssh/config. Put it before any "Host \*" section yourself otherwise:
ssh takes the first value it finds for a setting, and these say that
nothing of yours (your SSH agent, X11) is forwarded to a session.

Each connection is an exec of sshd in the session through the cluster's
API, as mcloud (this binary, logged in as you) makes it. A login lands in
the session's work directory (/work). The settings name mcloud's own key
and a host key file mcloud writes from what the session says before every
connection, so ssh asks nothing the first time and refuses any other key.

What comes out of a session is the agent's to choose: scp and rsync copy
links and git's own files (.git), which mcloud sandbox cp and pull leave
behind.

```
mcloud sandbox ssh-config [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox ssh-config --install
mcloud sandbox ssh-config >> ~/.ssh/config.d/sandbox
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--install` |  | write it, and include it at the top of ~/.ssh/config |

## mcloud sandbox start

Start a session.

Start a session: a pod with Claude Code in it, named NAME (or
session-xxxxx). The first time, this also makes your sandbox, and asks for
your Claude token if you haven't set one.

--from copies a directory of yours into the session, and makes it where
the session's commands start: claude, prompt, shell and pull.

A session runs until you stop it, or for as long as --for says. Its files
(/work) exist as long as it does.

```
mcloud sandbox start [NAME] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox start
mcloud sandbox start refactor --from ./my-repo
mcloud sandbox start refactor --for 8h
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--for` duration | `0s` | end the session after this long, e.g. 8h (default: when you stop it) |
| `--from` string |  | a directory to copy into the session, and work in there |

## mcloud sandbox stop

End sessions; their files go with them.

End sessions. A session's pod and everything in its work directory are
deleted: bring out what you want to keep first (mcloud sandbox pull for
commits, mcloud sandbox cp for files).

```
mcloud sandbox stop SESSION... [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox stop refactor
mcloud sandbox stop --all
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` |  | every session of yours |

## mcloud sandbox token

The Claude token your sessions log in with.

Sessions log in to Claude with your subscription, through a token that
you set once and renew once a year. Run \`claude setup-token\` on your own machine (logged in to your Claude subscription) and give what it prints: a token for model requests only, good for a year.

The token is kept in your sandbox in the cluster, where only your sessions
(and the cluster's admins) can read it. It is in no repository. A session
reads it when it starts: after a change, running sessions keep the old one.

| Command | |
| --- | --- |
| [`mcloud sandbox token set`](#mcloud-sandbox-token-set) | Set the token; it comes from stdin (or a hidden prompt) |
| [`mcloud sandbox token unset`](#mcloud-sandbox-token-unset) | Remove the token; new sessions can't start without one |

## mcloud sandbox token set

Set the token; it comes from stdin (or a hidden prompt).

```
mcloud sandbox token set
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud sandbox token set                 # asks for it
op read op://vault/claude/token | mcloud sandbox token set
```

## mcloud sandbox token unset

Remove the token; new sessions can't start without one.

```
mcloud sandbox token unset
```
